Use case: stylized-concept. Generate a seamless square material ALBEDO texture of traditional Korean fired grey clay roof tile. The attached canonical hanok artwork is the reference for premium understated hand-painted architectural illustration style and the charcoal/slate-grey ceramic palette. Do NOT depict a roof, tile shapes, ridges, individual tiles or tile seams. Fill the whole square with one uninterrupted matte fired-clay surface, flat orthographic view, fully diffuse neutral illumination, no lighting gradient, no edge-darkening, no highlights or cast shadows. A restrained medium-dark slate grey with a faint warm charcoal undertone, irregular fine clay grains and pores, faint soft wisps from hand pressing, small cloudy kiln variation, occasional tiny grey mineral specks. Low contrast, gently varied, not solid black and not bright white. No dramatic chips, no cracks, no terracotta orange, no glazed shine, no metallic finish, no marble veins, no geometric repeating pattern, no large spots, no lettering. This is a neutral base color map for actual curved overlapping 3D tiles; the geometry and scene light provide tile shape, depth, edges and shadows. All edges must tile seamlessly. The surface represents roughly 70cm by 70cm; keep clay pores and pigments fine, legible but restrained.
